claims.summary: Repeatedly sent tribute to the Tang court as Khitan territory grew.
Exploited Central Plains turmoil and an undefended northern border to nibble away neighboring commanderies.
Drove the Tatars, Xi, and Shiwei into service; clan tents flourished and they raided from time to time.
Begged an alliance and paid bribes to recover Prince Shili after Liu Shouguang refused a ransom of five thousand horses.
Selected generals, trained troops, crossed Zhaxing Ridge in autumn, and burned border grass after frost to starve Khitan horses.
Accepted fine horses as a bribe and sold the Khitan grazing land.

claims.assessment: dissolute and extravagant in later years

claims.summary: In his late years withdrew to dwell on Great Peace Mountain.
Feigned peace, feasted Khitan tribes outside the walls, then sprang hidden troops and seized Prince Shili.
Refused the tribes' offer of five thousand horses to ransom Prince Shili.

claims.assessment: harsh and cruel in his last years

claims.summary: In his last years cruelty drove soldiers to desert and enter the Khitan.
Led ten thousand Khitan horsemen against Liu Shouguang at Pingzhou.
Seized at a feigned feast and taken into the city.
Recovered after Qinde sued for peace and paid bribes.
Replaced Qinde as lord when Qinde's power waned.
Supplanted Qinde as chief.
Relied on strength, refused the three-year tribal rotation, and styled himself lord of the state.
Invaded Yunzhong in force in Tianyou 4.
Met the Martial Emperor at Yunzhong, feasted in the tent, and pledged brotherhood.
Agreed to winter campaign plans and left three thousand horses in return for lavish gifts.
Sent envoys with famous horses, female musicians, and sable pelts seeking investiture from the Liang founder.

claims.summary: Promised to send cavalry to relieve Luzhou, then stopped when Luzhou was already pacified.
In the eighth month of year thirteen led tribes claiming a million men, took Zhenwu from Lin and Sheng, and drove through Yun and Shuo.
Death announced to Abaoji when Zhuangzong first succeeded.
Sent envoys, met Abaoji face to face, feasted him, and pledged brotherhood, asking for twenty thousand picked cavalry to recover Bian and Luo.
Rejected attendants' advice to capture Abaoji, refusing to break faith with tribal allies while rebels remained undestroyed, and sent him away with full ceremony.

claims.assessment: would not break faith with tribal allies

claims.summary: Established his reign title as founder of Liang.
Wrote offering immediate investiture if Abaoji would drive picked troops to Xinzhuang and destroy the Taiyuan foe.
First succeeded to the throne after his father's death.
Sent envoys to announce his father's death, offered gold and silks, and asked for cavalry to relieve Luzhou.
Marched from Dai to relieve the northern frontier; the Khitan host then withdrew.
Sent Emperor Mingzong, Li Cunshen, and Yan Bao to lead troops that lifted the siege of Youzhou.
Attacked and besieged Youzhou.
Struck Lu Wenjin with troops; Wenjin fared ill and fled to the Khitan.
Led thirty thousand to punish Wenjin; Khitan horsemen relieved Xinzhou and Dewei was routed, his army nearly annihilated.
Pressed by his troops, killed Li Cunju at Qigou Pass and turned back to attack Xin and Wu.
Beaten by Zhou Dewei, fled to the Khitan and led them to take Xinzhou.
Killed by Lu Wenjin at Qigou Pass.
Sent with Li Cunshen and Yan Bao to lead troops that lifted the siege of Youzhou.
Led troops with Emperor Mingzong and Yan Bao to rescue Youzhou and lift the siege.
Led troops with Emperor Mingzong and Li Cunshen to rescue Youzhou and lift the siege.
Murdered his lord Wang Rong in the tenth month of year eighteen.

claims.assessment: a groom's lackey / menial petty man

claims.summary: Murdered by Zhang Wenli.
Marched to punish Zhang Wenli after Wang Rong's murder.
Refused advice to lift the siege of Zhenzhou and withdraw from the Khitan.
Personally led five thousand armored horsemen, burst from Mulberry Grove, and scattered the Khitan vanguard of ten thousand.
Camped at Dingzhou, next day fought Xi chief Tuonuo, was surrounded, and charged in and out of the ring four times.
Brought back to safety by Li Sizhao.
Pursued Abaoji's northward retreat with elite cavalry and praised Khitan camp discipline.
Reached Youzhou, sent two hundred scouts who were all captured, and turned back.
Joined Zhang Wenli's plot and sent Wang Yu to bring the Khitan as allies.
Sent by Wang Chuzhi to bring the Khitan in as reinforcements.
Poured across the frontier in the twelfth month and besieged Youzhou.
After horses foundered on thin Sha River ice, fell back to Wangdu.
Summoned Lu Wenjin, pointed to Heaven, and said Heaven had not willed him to come this far, then led the army north.
Proclaimed himself emperor and created offices on the Chinese model.
Raised walled cities and palaces in the northern steppe three thousand li from Youzhou; named the capital Western Tower, doors facing east.
Built a separate city south of the capital to house Han subjects, with three Buddhist temples and a thousand monks and nuns.
During Tongguang harbored ambition to open territory but feared Bohai would strike his rear.
In year three marched against Bohai Liaodong and left Tunei and Lu Wenjin to hold Ying and Ping and raid Yan and Ji.

claims.assessment: grew up on the frontier / frontier barbarian

claims.summary: Held Youzhou with the garrison against Abaoji's siege.
Captured when the Khitan took Zhuo commandery.
Sent envoys in urgent appeal after the Khitan crossed the Sha River at Xinle.
At the founding of Tang, when Turks raided to the north bank of the Wei, wanted to abandon Chang'an for Fan and Deng.

claims.statement: Chinese writes 太守 where the speech's speaker is Tang Taizong (太宗); English renders Taizong.

claims.summary: Within a few years captured both Turk khans and made them palace guards.

claims.assessment: bold in war / heroic and martial

claims.summary: Aspired to destroy the Xiongnu as a Han court general.
Met Zhuangzong with five thousand horsemen and surrounded his personal guard.
Hearing Zhuangzong was in peril, rode forward in tears, broke the enemy line, and brought him back.
Summoned by Abaoji, who told him Heaven had not willed the campaign to go farther.
Ordered with Tunei to hold Ying, Ping and neighboring prefectures and raid Yan and Ji while Abaoji attacked Bohai.
Ordered with Lu Wenjin to hold Ying, Ping and raid Yan and Ji.
First took the throne after Zhuangzong's death; officers pressed him when the capital had no lord.
Sent Yao Kun with a letter announcing mourning.

Granted Deguang a memorial stele for Abaoji and sent rich gifts including necklaces and brocades to Deguang's mother.
Carried Mingzong's mourning letter to Western Tower, then on to Shenzhou where Abaoji was campaigning in Bohai.

claims.summary: Accompanied Lady Shulü's funeral train toward Western Tower, received word of the death, and returned.

claims.summary: Understood Chinese but dared not speak it openly lest the tribes grow soft.
Three sons, all imposing men.
Was in Bohai when Yao Kun arrived; had mustered fifty thousand horsemen intending to aid Zhuangzong but could not leave Bohai unconquered.

sourceDate.text: 天成元年七月二十七日

claims.summary: Fell ill with fever three days after Kun arrived; a great star fell before his tent; died on Tiancheng 1/7/27 at Fuyu.
Received Kun in the domed tent with his wife on a facing couch, questioned him at length, and offered a personal alliance at Youzhou.

claims.assessment: Zhuangzong wasted the people with palace women, musicians, hunting, and wine until the realm turned against him

claims.summary: Installed by his mother as tribal chief to oversee the state; the tribes had long obeyed him.
Sent Molin and more than thirty others to renew relations and seek a stele for his father.
Had been expected to succeed and was serving in Bohai; replaced there by Anduan when Deguang was installed.
Sent by his mother to Bohai to replace Tuyu.
Led more than thirty envoys to Mingzong to renew friendly relations.
Proclaimed the Tianxian era in year three.
Took Pingzhou and sent Tunei to relieve Wang Du at Zhongshan.
Sent the Tiyiin with seven thousand horsemen to relieve Dingzhou.
Led fifty thousand through Yanmen to Jinyang and routed Zhang Jingda the same day.
Enthroned the Jin founder as Great Jin Emperor, pledged a father-son state, and received Youzhou circuit plus Xin, Wu, Yun, Ying, and Shuo and an annual silk tribute.
Put Zhao Dejun and Zhao Yanshou in fetters to follow his camp.
Changed Tianxian 11 to Huitong 1, made Zhao Yanshou Grand Councilor, elevated Youzhou to Southern Capital.
If the slightest request went unmet he sent rebukes; the Jin founder always humbled himself.
Rebelled at Dingzhou and sought Khitan aid.
Rebellion crushed the following year.
Sent with five thousand horsemen to aid Wang Du; defeated by Wang Yanqiu at Quyang.
Died in the Dingzhou campaign; the Khitan later sought his bones.

Captured and beheaded after Wang Du fell.
Asked Deguang to enthrone him, with the Shi clan keeping Taiyuan.
Mingzong, angered at the deceit, beheaded him.
Appointed the Jin founder military governor of Hedong and northern commander when the Khitan pressed Yunzhou.
Kept sending envoys with reports while Tuyu was at the Tang court.

Besieged by Zhang Jingda, sent He Fu with a memorial begging Khitan troops and offering to become a vassal.
Entered Luoyang and sent Chancellor Zhao Ying to thank the Khitan.

claims.assessment: courted the Khitan with extreme deference throughout his reign, almost no rupture

claims.summary: Killed by Yang Guangyuan and others who then surrendered to the Khitan.
Killed Zhang Jingda and surrendered to the Khitan.

claims.assessment: deeply ashamed at Deguang's jest about eating ten thousand war horses

claims.summary: Succeeded without first reporting to Deguang; letters omitted vassal language.
Demoted to Marquis Who Betrayed Righteousness and sent to Huanglong Prefecture.
Sent sons Yanshu and Yanbao with surrender memorial and imperial seal.
Furious the Young Emperor took the throne without leave; insulted Jin envoys.
Marched south, took Qizhou, reached the Yellow River; defeated at Yangcheng in the third month and fled to Youzhou on a camel.
Flogged chiefs for the Yangcheng rout; only Zhao Yanshou was spared.
Entered Bian, occupied the palace, demoted the Young Emperor, appointed Jin officials, proclaimed Great Liao.
Reported Jing Yanguang's war threat to Deguang.

claims.summary: Proclaimed his reign at Jinyang on the fifteenth day.
Died on the twenty-first day of the fourth month, aged 46, after 22 years ruling the Khitan; a star fell on the 18th.

claims.assessment: Deguang's words were evasive; he is near death

claims.summary: Proclaimed successor as Prince Yongkang; led tribes home on the 21st, changed Huitong 10 to Tianlu 1, styled Emperor Heaven-Granted.
Killed Taining, seized the throne, proclaimed Yingli 1, styled Emperor Heaven-Compliant.
Prepared a southern raid with Yang Yan; routed by Zhou Shizong at Gaoping.

translationRepairs: For generations they lived in the Liao marshes on the south bank of the Huang River. Yumen Pass lay eleven hundred li to their south, and Youzhou another seven hundred li beyond the pass — lands that had once belonged to the Xianbei.

For generations they lived in the Liao marshes on the south bank of the Huang River. Yuguan lay eleven hundred li to their south, and Youzhou another seven hundred li beyond the pass — lands that had once belonged to the Xianbei.
榆關 is Yuguan near Shanhaiguan, not Yumen Pass in the Hexi Corridor.

For generations they dwelt amid the Liao marshes, on the south bank of the Huang River; one thousand one hundred li south to Yumen Pass, and seven hundred li south from Yumen Pass to Youzhou — the old territory of the Xianbei.

For generations they dwelt amid the Liao marshes, on the south bank of the Huang River; one thousand one hundred li south to Yuguan, and seven hundred li south from Yuguan to Youzhou — the old territory of the Xianbei.
The literal field repeats the same confusion of 榆關 with 玉門關; Yuguan is correct.
Emperor Wenzong was heroic and martial; within a few years he captured both Turks and made them palace guards.
Emperor Taizong was heroic and martial; within a few years he captured both Turks and made them palace guards.
文皇 refers here to Tang Taizong, as the surrounding passage and idiomatic field establish. Emperor Taizong is clearer than the ambiguous posthumous-style rendering Emperor Wen.

The Chief Commander north of the river, Lord Ling — recently because of the Weizhou military mutiny the late emperor issued an edict ordering his punishment; once he heard of internal troubles, the army and masses lost heart, and when the capital had no lord, high and low firmly enthroned Lord Ling and asked him to preside over the altars of soil and grain — he has now followed the people's hope and ascended the imperial throne."

The Chief Commander north of the river, Lord Ling — recently because of the Weizhou military mutiny the late emperor issued an edict ordering him to suppress it; once he heard of internal troubles, the army and masses lost heart, and when the capital had no lord, high and low firmly enthroned Lord Ling and asked him to preside over the altars of soil and grain — he has now followed the people's hope and ascended the imperial throne."
詔令除討 says the late emperor ordered Lord Ling to suppress the Weizhou mutiny, not that he ordered Lord Ling punished.

At that time Zhao Dejun of Youzhou encamped at Tuanbai Valley, sent envoys to the tent headquarters, asked to be enthroned himself with the Shi clan hereditarily holding Taiyuan; Deguang answered the envoy, pointing at a stone before the tent: "I have already pledged brotherhood with Lord Stone — when stone rots it may change."

At that time Zhao Dejun of Youzhou encamped at Tuanbai Valley, sent envoys to the tent headquarters, asked to be enthroned himself with the Shi clan hereditarily holding Taiyuan; Deguang answered the envoy, pointing at a stone before the tent: "I have already pledged a father-and-son alliance with Lord Stone — when stone rots it may change."
父子之盟 explicitly denotes a father-and-son alliance, not brotherhood.
In Qingtai 3 the Jin founder was besieged by Zhang Jingda and others. He sent Commander He Fuben with a petition begging for Khitan aid and offering to become their vassal.
In Qingtai 3 the Jin founder was besieged by Zhang Jingda and others. He sent Commander He Fu with a petition begging for Khitan aid and offering to become their vassal.
The commander's name is 何福, He Fu; 賫 is the following verb meaning that he carried the memorial.

In the third month of year two he ordered Xuzhou military governor Wang Yanchao and others to build fortifications at Li Yankou. They fought several thousand Khitan horsemen at Anping county and defeated them.) 〉

In the third month of the second year he ordered Xu Prefecture military governor Wang Yanchao and others to build fortifications at Li Yankou. They fought several thousand Khitan horsemen at Anping County and defeated them.
許州 is Xu Prefecture, not Xuzhou (徐州). The revision also removes closing Chinese editorial marks that were accidentally copied into the English sentence.
